heading: What you might see
intro: The species Teresa's own walk notes name. Interpretation of flora, fauna, geology and history is part of every walk, and no two days show the same things.

items.label: Albert's Lyrebird
items.detail: Elusive, and heard more than seen in the rainforest along the border ranges.

items.label: Glossy Black Cockatoo
items.detail: Feeding in the she oaks along the foothills track to the Lower Portals, with luck.

items.label: Peregrine falcon
items.detail: Nesting on the cave dotted cliffs of Campbell's Folly, outliers of Mt Barney.

items.label: Rock wallaby
items.detail: On the same rhyolite cliffs, along with plants found nowhere else.

items.label: Wildflowers
items.detail: Fringe lilies and orchids in the eucalypt forest and along the paddock edges in spring.

items.label: Fungi
items.detail: Bright fungi on fallen timber after rain, a favourite stop on rainforest walks.
items.alt: A yellow fungus on a log

items.label: Tiny brightly coloured spiders
items.detail: The small things a guide stops for, like the brightly coloured spider a walker found on a Scenic Rim day walk.
items.alt: A close up of an insect on a leaf

items.label: 136 bird species
items.detail: Recorded in the Flinders Goolman Conservation Estate, with 25 mammals, 13 reptiles and 531 plant species.
